entry.title: The Circular Shield — How the Attorney Grievance Commission Protects the Attorneys Who Protect the Enterprise
entry.content:
What Happened

On or about September 27, 2026, a Request for Investigation was filed with the Michigan Attorney Grievance Commission against two attorneys:

  1. Lamar Moreland — Assistant Attorney General. Serves as Vice Chair of the Purpose Charter Academy Board of Directors. Works in the AG’s Criminal Justice Bureau — the bureau that prosecutes state RICO under MCL 750.159i. Governs the school the AG should be investigating.

  2. Todd Perkins — Brian Banks’ personal attorney. Filed the PPO (Case No. 26-114083-PH) to silence the complainant. Has 4 personal bankruptcies and $100K+ in IRS tax liens. His brothers are Judge Sean Perkins (36th District Court) and Judge David Perkins (Probate Court, Chief Judge Pro Tem).

On October 1, 2026, the AGC responded.

The Response — AGC File No. 26-2141

Cynthia C. Bullington, Assistant Deputy Administrator, sent the following:

“We received the enclosed correspondence, in which you list more than one attorney. You must complete a separate form for each attorney describing what actions by that attorney you believe constitute misconduct.”

“Your original correspondence is enclosed. No further action will be taken until you resubmit the Request for Investigation with the requested information.”

They returned the original evidence. They sent blank forms. They created a file number — 26-2141 — and closed it before it opened.

Michael V. Goetz, Grievance Administrator, signed the cover letter enclosing the blank Request for Investigation forms.

Why This Matters: The Circular Shield

The AGC is the entity that disciplines attorneys in Michigan. It operates under the authority of the Michigan Supreme Court (MCR 9.109 et seq.). When an attorney violates the Michigan Rules of Professional Conduct, the AGC investigates, and if warranted, files formal charges with the Attorney Discipline Board.

But the AGC is also a gate. And when the gate chooses not to open, every attorney behind it is shielded.

Here is the circle:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   THE CIRCULAR SHIELD                     │
│                                                          │
│  BANKS operates the enterprise                           │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  PERKINS (Banks' attorney) files PPO to silence          │
│  complainant                                             │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  MORELAND (AAG) governs the school from the board,       │
│  preventing AG investigation                             │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  Complainant files AGC complaint against Perkins         │
│  AND Moreland                                            │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  AGC BOUNCES IT — "you listed more than one attorney"    │
│  Returns evidence. Sends blank forms.                    │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  Enterprise continues. 362 children lose another day.    │
│    ↓                                                     │
│  (Loop back to top)                                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Every entity that could break the circle passes the complaint to another entity that also won’t act:

EntityCould Break the Circle ByWhat They Actually Did
AG (Nessel)Investigating Banks under consumer protection, nonprofit fraud, or state RICOSILENCE. Her own employee (Moreland) sits on the board.
AGCInvestigating Moreland for conflict of interest (MRPC 1.7, 1.11, 8.4) and Perkins for frivolous PPO (MRPC 3.1)BOUNCED. “File separate forms.” Returned evidence.
CourtsDenying the PPO against protected speechENTERED IT. Judge Abraham signed it. Perkins’ brothers are judges in Wayne County.
JTCDisciplining connected judges (Miller, Yancey, Ramsey, Sean Perkins, David Perkins)Investigations opened but confidential. No public action.
MDERevoking Banks’ credentials, emergency charter reviewAcknowledged Oct 1. No action since.
SBEDirecting MDE to act, ordering charter reviewSILENCE. All 8 members notified by name.
DPSCDEmergency charter review as authorizerSILENCE.

The circle is complete. No entity acts because every entity defers to another entity that also won’t act. The attorneys protect the enterprise. The AGC protects the attorneys. The AG protects the AGC. The courts protect the AG. And the children pay.

This is not a random group of strangers who happened to bounce a complaint. This is a network of professionals connected to the same institutions, the same offices, the same courts, and the same legal community as the attorneys they were asked to investigate.

What the Rules Actually Say

From the AGC’s own process document (enclosed in their response to Kevin):

Michael V. Goetz doesn’t need a complaint from Kevin Mok. He doesn’t need two separate forms. He doesn’t need anything except the facts — and the facts are public. What Compliance Looks Like vs. What Happened

entry.title: The One-Way Door — Purpose Charter Academy's Access Denial Pattern
entry.content:
Two Staff. Two Incidents. One Policy.

Incident 1 — August 29, 2026 (Physical)

A parent with legal custody arrived at Purpose Charter Academy, 10101 East Canfield, Detroit.

Giselle — the receptionist — denied the parent access to their child.

Brian Roderick Banks — the school’s operator — told Detroit Police officers he is “an attorney.” He is not an attorney. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He has 9 criminal convictions (6 felony), including assault with intent to murder.

The police escorted the parent off school property based on Banks’ false representation.

DPD Report #26-0909-0176. The report exists. The badge numbers exist. The custody order exists.

Incident 2 — October 12, 2026 (Phone)

A caller dialed (313) 767-3100 — Purpose Charter Academy’s main line.

Ms. Perkins — the receptionist — answered.

The caller asked about Banks and DaSean.

Ms. Perkins stated:

  • She has not seen Banks today
  • She has not seen DaSean today
  • She has not seen anybody

School is in session. She is at the reception desk. She answered the phone. She is not blind.

She lied.

The caller has called before. This is not the first contact.

The Pattern

DateStaffMethodWhat they saidTruth
Aug 29GiselleIn person[Banks]: “I am an attorney”He has never been admitted to any bar. 9 convictions.
Oct 12Ms. PerkinsPhone“Haven’t seen Banks, haven’t seen DaSean, haven’t seen anybody”School in session. She’s at the desk. She answered the phone.

Two staff members. 44 days apart. Same conduct: deny that anyone is present, deny access to the child.

This is not two individuals making personal choices. This is institutional policy. Someone trained them. Someone told them what to say.

The One-Way Door

Purpose Charter Academy is a one-way door:

What goes INWhat stays OUT
Public education dollars ($4.9M/yr)Parents with custody rights
Children (enrolled by parents who trust the school)Information about those children
72.67% of revenue → The Purpose Group LLCAccountability
Board members (a judge, an AAG, a council member)Oversight

The receptionist is the membrane. She is the operational layer between a parent and their child. On August 29, Giselle was that membrane. On October 12, Ms. Perkins is.

The name at the desk changes. The policy doesn’t.

The Perkins Question

Ms. Perkins at the PCA reception desk shares a surname with three people already documented in the network:

Todd PerkinsBanks’ personal attorneyPerkins Law Group, Detroit. Represented Judge Miller in DTW gun case.
Judge Sean Perkins36th District CourtTodd’s brother. Worked at Todd’s firm before the bench.

Three Perkins in the legal/judicial layer protecting Banks. One Perkins at the school reception desk denying access to a parent.

Is Ms. Perkins related to Todd and Sean Perkins?

We don’t know yet. The surname match is documented. The question is asked. The answer will come from the sweep.

What the Law Says

FERPA (20 U.S.C. §1232g): Custodial parents have the right to access their children’s education records and information about their children at school.

MCL 380.1137: Schools shall not deny a parent access to their child except by court order.

MCL 600.916: It is illegal to represent yourself as an attorney if you are not one. Banks did this on August 29 to justify denying access. DPD Report #26-0909-0176 documents it.

A receptionist saying “I haven’t seen anybody” is not a legal basis for denying a parent information about their child. It is a lie designed to end the conversation.

entry.title: Anderson Localization — When Courts Trap Cases
entry.content:
Lens: 🕸️ Topology ⚛️ Lattice 📅 Chronology 💰 Money ⚖️ Legal 🏛️ Capture

The Physics

In 1958, physicist Philip W. Anderson showed that disorder in a crystal lattice prevents electrons from propagating. Instead of flowing through the material, electrons become trapped — localized — near the defect sites. The stronger the disorder, the shorter the distance an electron can travel before it stops.

This is not a metaphor. It is a mathematical identity.

Replace lattice sites with court divisions. Replace electrons with cases. Replace disorder potential with captured judges. The same equation applies: cases entering a disordered judicial system cannot propagate to a fair hearing. They localize.

The Lattice

Rendered by petalTongue — heatmap, bar chart, and faceted gauges via the grammar-of-graphics scene compiler.

The Measurement: Localization Length (ξ)

In physics, the localization length ξ measures how far an electron can travel through a disordered lattice before it becomes trapped. The formula:

ξ = −1 / ln(1 − p)

Where p is the probability of encountering a captured judge on any given bench that handles that case type.

  • ξ < 5 → Strongly localized. A case has almost no chance of receiving an independent hearing.
  • 5 ≤ ξ < 10 → Moderately localized. Some paths exist, but most lead through captured benches.
  • ξ > 10 → Weakly localized. Capture exists but is diluted across enough judges.

What the Numbers Mean

Probate: The Deepest Trap (ξ = 3.5)

Wayne County Probate has 4 judges. One of them — David Perkins — is Chief Judge Pro Tem, meaning he has case assignment authority. He decides which judge hears which probate, guardianship, conservatorship, and estate case.

A 25% random capture ratio becomes much worse when the captured judge controls the docket. This is not random disorder — it is engineered disorder. Perkins can route cases to himself.

This matters because the Banks network operates Serenity Guardianship Services within Probate Court’s jurisdiction. Banks has 9 criminal convictions. He has never been barred from guardianship work.

36th District: Concentration Attack (ξ = 7.2)

Three captured judges — Yancey, Adam Sabree, Sean Perkins — all elected November 2022, all taking their benches January 1, 2023. This was a coordinated bench capture: three seats in one election cycle, all connected to the same network.

The 36th District handles misdemeanors, traffic, small claims, and preliminary examinations for felonies. That last category matters most: a preliminary exam determines whether a felony case proceeds to Circuit Court. A captured preliminary exam judge can dismiss or bind over based on network loyalty rather than evidence.

Guardianship: The Cross-Court Trap (ξ = 5.5)

Guardianship cases can be heard in either Family Division (Aliyah Sabree) or Probate Court (David Perkins). Both benches have captured judges. There is no path through the Wayne County guardianship system that avoids a captured bench.

This is the judicial equivalent of total localization — the case cannot propagate to a fair hearing regardless of which court it enters.

In the physics, Anderson localization has a critical dimension: in 1D and 2D, any amount of disorder causes localization. Only in 3D can electrons sometimes avoid traps.

Wayne County’s court system is effectively 1D for most case types — there is only one bench that handles each type. For guardianship, it is 2D (two benches), but both are captured. There is no third dimension. There is no escape path.

What Would Fix It

Anderson localization disappears when disorder is removed. The judicial equivalent:

  1. Recusal — Captured judges recuse from all cases touching the Banks network
  2. Reassignment — Chief judges reassign network-connected cases to independent benches
  3. Federal jurisdiction — Cases move to a different lattice entirely (U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Michigan)

Options 1 and 2 require the captured judges to acknowledge their connections. The documented evidence shows they have not done so.

Option 3 is the Anderson localization equivalent of increasing dimensionality — adding new propagation channels that bypass the disordered sites entirely.
